subject: Packaging options and downgrade/upgrade path for Alpine Health
messages:
From: Sam Kline <sam.k@alpinehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging options for pilot -> production

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. We're kicking off internal planning for a Q4 pilot and want to understand packaging: if we start on Hosted API for the pilot and later want to move to Dedicated capacity, what's the upgrade path? Conversely, if capacity needs shrink, how do downgrades work without big penalties? Also trying to get clarity on bundling Redwood Optimize and any available commitments/discounts for a 12-month term.

High level details that would help:
- Typical timing to switch from Hosted to Dedicated (assume 200-500 vCPU / 4-8 GPU equivalent workload)
- Any minimum committed spend for discounts / what tiers exist
- Whether Optimize is billed separately and if it can be bundled into a reserved commitment
- Downgrade/change windows and whether credits are prorated

cc: procurement (procurement@alpinehealth.com)

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Kline
VP, Product Engineering
Alpine Health
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Kline <sam.k@alpinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for pilot -> production

Sam — appreciate the quick follow-up and great to hear the demo resonated. Attaching a short packaging playbook and a preliminary quote so you have concrete numbers. High-level answers below; I can sync with procurement for contract language if helpful.

Attachments: Redwood_Packaging_Playbook_v1.pdf, pricing-quote-AlpineHealth.xlsx

Quick summary:
- Hosted -> Dedicated: typical transition is 4–6 weeks once we agree on committed capacity and network setup (VPC peering, certs). For your scale (200–500 vCPU equivalent, expected to map to ~4–8 GPUs), planning and procurement are the longest pieces; actual model migration is low-risk.
- Commit & discounts: discount tiers start at a $150k ARR commit for 12 months (5% off list), step to 10% at $500k, and 15% at $1.2M. We can mix usage and reserved credits — the quote shows blended unit prices.
- Redwood Optimize: typically add-on but we can include it in the reserved commitment (counted as a % add-on). If you commit, Optimize licenses transfer to the reserved capacity and the effective discount applies to the bundle.
- Downgrade path: downgrades are allowed at the next billing cycle with 30 days' notice. We do not charge exit penalties; unused committed credits are handled via stepdown credits on a sliding schedule (see playbook for examples).

If it helps, I'd like to run the numbers with Rachel on discounts and Marissa for the Dedicated sizing + operational runbook. Available Thursday for a call?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Packaging options for pilot -> production — need pricing/ops guidance

Rachel/Marissa — forwarding Sam's questions (Alpine Health, deal ALP-4592). Please see the attached draft quote. Key asks: stepdown schedule example, billing presentation (single invoice vs separate lines), SLA differences between Hosted vs Dedicated, and any flexibility on 12-mo tier thresholds. My proposed answers below — please correct and sign off. Also flag anything that should go to legal/procurement early.

Proposed answers:
- Stepdown: 12-mo commit with monthly reconciliation. If committed $600k and actual run rate falls to $300k month 7, we apply stepdown credits: 50% of unused credits convert to service credits over 3 months, and there is a 60-day rev-rec smoothing period. (Need finance to confirm precise percentage.)
- SLA: Hosted standard SLA (99.5% uptime), Dedicated SLA can be 99.9% for an enterprise package; add-on premium SLA available for 99.95%.
- Billing: prefer single invoice with line-item detail for chargeback; procurement sometimes requests separate invoices — we can support separate lines in the invoice but prefer one payment instrument.

Rachel — can you validate the stepdown percentages with finance? Marissa — confirm provisioning timeline and any additional onboarding credits we can offer for the pilot.

Thanks,
Sean

To: Sam Kline <sam.k@alpinehealth.com>, Alpine Health Procurement <procurement@alpinehealth.com>

Date: 2026-07-08T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for pilot -> production

Sam — following up with concrete answers after internal review. Apologies for the delay; wanted to confirm with finance and ops. See below and attached updated quote + SOW draft.

Attachments: pricing-quote-AlpineHealth.xlsx, SOW-AlpineHealth-draft.docx

Finalized answers:
- Upgrade timing (Hosted -> Dedicated): 4–6 weeks post contract signature assuming timely network setup. We’ll run a parallel validation on a subset of traffic during week 1 of onboarding to ensure parity.
- Commit discounts: confirmed — 5% at $150k ARR, 10% at $500k, 15% at $1.2M. We can offer a one-time additional 2% strategic partner discount if you sign within 30 days and include a marketing case study.
- Stepdown schedule example (confirmed with finance): for a 12-mo $600k commit that drops to $300k mid-term: 60% of the delta is returned as account credit distributed over the remaining term; the remainder is recognized as revenue. That credit can be applied to future usage or to Optimize seats. We can bake a 90-day stepdown smoothing if you need slower amortization.
- SLA differences: Hosted (standard) 99.5% uptime; Dedicated (enterprise) 99.9%; add-on premium 99.95% (requires Dedicated + capacity reservation). All SLAs include incident response SLAs and regular postmortems for Sev1s.
- Billing: we will issue a single invoice with line-item breakout (capacity, Optimize, support) — procurement can map to internal chargeback codes. If procurement requires separate invoices, we can accommodate as a special billing arrangement.
- Downgrades: allowed at next billing cycle with 30 days' notice. No exit penalty. Unused committed credits handled per stepdown schedule above.

Pilot support offer: for pilots that convert to Dedicated we can provide a one-week onboarding credit (equivalent to $8k in hosted consumption) and a discounted Optimize seat for the pilot period.

Next steps: if this aligns, procurement can review the attached SOW and I'll get legal to prepare an MSA + order form. Proposal validity: 30 days.

Would you like me to loop legal/procurement on Redwood's side for a short call next week?

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
